Jmk7o1aFd-4.speaker: adnan
Jmk7o1aFd-4.speaker_note: Describes being raised in Syria and his twelve years in the city, and gives his own list of lessons.
Jmk7o1aFd-4.title: Lessons Learned From a Year of Blood
Jmk7o1aFd-4.one_line: Seven lessons from a year of war on Gaza: gratitude, a living ummah, youth, advocacy, no saviours, leadership, and education with civil disagreement.
Jmk7o1aFd-4.summary: He marks a year of war on Gaza with seven lessons he has personally drawn, framed by Yusuf 12:111 on learning from stories. He refuses to date the story from last October rather than 1948, and says the dead, likely near 100,000, will not have died in vain only if those left behind learn. First, his own problems are trivial; on Thanksgiving weekend he reminds people that the Prophet's ummah are the people of praise, and gratitude means serving the underserved. Second, the ummah his generation gave up on after the Arab Spring is weak but alive in people's hearts. Third, youth are the key to an awakening, as the campus protests proved and as the Prophet's young companions show, so institutions must invest in them. Fourth, Muslims must sit on the boards and committees that shape policy; raised in Syria to keep his head down, he tells youth to ignore his cynicism. Fifth, no saviour is coming from the powers that invaded Iraq; Muslims must value Muslim blood first, as the Prophet did at Mu'tah. Sixth, without leadership a community is only a population. Seventh, education and civil disagreement are the way out, so set aside the 1% Muslims disagree on.

outline.heading: Opening
Lessons from stories
outline.gist: Yusuf 12:111: the Quran's stories are not bedtime tales but real events that teach people of understanding about their own lives, with guidance and mercy.

outline.heading: The story began in 1948
outline.gist: He refuses to give significance to any day of last October or after; the oppression began in 1948, within living memory, and arguing over later dates loses the bigger picture.

outline.heading: A year of blood, and deaths that must not be in vain
outline.gist: A full year of daily bloodshed in the Holy Land, mostly women and children, cannot leave us unaffected; the real toll is near 100,000 and rising. As a young cancer death drives research, these deaths are not in vain only if those left behind learn; he offers what he personally has learned.

outline.heading: Lesson one: my problems are overrated
outline.gist: His worries as a citizen of a first-world country are trivial next to what is happening elsewhere. Compare yourself with the millions who have less, not the few who have more, as the Prophet taught.

outline.heading: The people of praise: gratitude through service
outline.gist: On Thanksgiving weekend: Muslims need no special day, since this ummah is known for praise and the Prophet carries the banner of praise. See what Allah gave rather than percentages; the gift brings the responsibility to serve the underserved and be their voice.

outline.heading: Lesson two: the ummah is still alive
outline.gist: His generation lost hope in the ummah in the mid-2010s after the Arab Spring backfired. This year proved the body still feels the pain of its limbs, though it cannot yet react: the ummah is a concept alive in hearts, shown by millions worldwide, despite tyrants and division.

outline.heading: Lesson three: the youth are the key
outline.gist: The key to a modern awakening is the youth, who proved in schools, universities and streets that they are braver than his generation, which lives in survival mode and wants its children only safe and studying the safest thing.

outline.heading: The Prophet built on the young; so must we
outline.gist: Institutions and speakers must give the youth time, place and resources, as the Prophet did with a nucleus mostly under 21. Young people must feel their historic role, and parents must tell their children they are the ummah's future.

outline.heading: The campuses moved public opinion
outline.gist: The spontaneous campus protests worldwide, including in this city, were something he never thought possible. Students were brutalized and lost placements yet stood their ground, and they, not countries or politicians, moved public opinion.

outline.heading: Lesson four: be where policy is made
outline.gist: Muslims must be involved in social and political advocacy, present on every senate, board or committee that shapes internal or external policy.

outline.heading: Raised to walk beside the wall
outline.gist: Raised in Syria to keep his head down and go through life undetected, a mistake that cost his generation and the region dearly, he still believes politics is only corrupt people and cannot rewire his brain at 39.

outline.heading: Ignore my cynicism: get a seat on the boards
outline.gist: Young people should ignore him on politics and get inside the system. Muslims complain endlessly about schools but have no one on the public or Catholic school boards to say what goes against Muslim identity; get involved, civilly, without division and fighting.

outline.heading: Interlude
Lesson five: nothing scratches your itch like your own nail
outline.gist: The ummah's short memory is mind-blowing: expecting rescue from the same countries and politicians who were murdering Muslims a decade or two ago would make sense only if all history before 2020 were wiped out.

outline.heading: Iraq 2003: no one is coming
outline.gist: The country some hope will intervene entered Iraq in 2003 and slaughtered people, some still missing twenty years later. Stop waiting for a saviour, Muslim or not: you are the saviour, or step aside.

outline.heading: Muslim blood valued by Muslims first: Mu'tah
outline.gist: Others will value Muslim blood only when Muslims value it first. When the Prophet's envoy was killed, he sent 3,000 men against a vast army at Mu'tah, the least rational military move in Arabia, because of the worth of one Muslim life.

outline.heading: Lesson six: without leadership, only a population
outline.gist: The missing link, in Muslim-majority and minority countries alike, is leadership; without it a community is a population with things in common. Giving several khutbahs in a day to a thousand, six hundred and three hundred students depresses him: so much skill and wealth, so little done.

outline.heading: Energy dispersed; even a bad leader beats none
outline.gist: Without leadership energy is never channelled and disperses into nothing, so we cannot move policy, media or laws. After twelve years of saying it he feels like a broken record; a leader going the wrong way at least hits a dead end and turns, unlike the headless chicken.

outline.heading: Lesson seven: education and critical thinking
outline.gist: He is fully convinced education is the way out: a well-informed population capable of critical thinking and productive dialogue will find its own solutions, and can disagree without starting a world war.

outline.heading: Hang your egos outside the masjid
outline.gist: We can no longer afford Muslims fighting Muslims while the ummah crumbles. Come in with service, humility and love for Allah, and work with others toward shared goals even if you dislike their methods or them.

outline.heading: Agree on 99%, shelve the 1%
outline.gist: Many listeners stop coming when he says what they dislike, yet no two people agree on everything. Muslims agree on 99% of life's biggest questions; set the 1% aside for a couple of decades and focus on youth, bringing people to the masjid and helping those who struggle.

outline.heading: So their deaths are not in vain
outline.gist: If we learn these lessons, the lack of support our brothers and sisters found in their distress will fuel a sustainable awakening in the ummah.

outline.heading: Outro

9:111.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱشۡتَرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَأَمۡوَٰلَهُم بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلۡجَنَّةَۚ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَيَقۡتُلُونَ وَيُقۡتَلُونَۖ وَعۡدًا عَلَيۡهِ حَقࣰّ ا فِي ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلِ وَٱلۡقُرۡءَانِۚ وَمَنۡ أَوۡفَىٰ بِعَهۡدِهِۦ مِنَ ٱللَّهِۚ فَٱسۡتَبۡشِرُواْ بِبَيۡعِكُمُ ٱلَّذِي بَايَعۡتُم بِهِۦۚ وَذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
9:111.en: Lo! Allah hath bought from the believers their lives and their wealth because the Garden will be theirs: they shall fight in the way of Allah and shall slay and be slain. It is a promise which is binding on Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an. Who fulfilleth His covenant better than Allah? Rejoice then in your bargain that ye have made, for that is the supreme triumph

kuGb1M-6KgU.speaker: adnan
kuGb1M-6KgU.speaker_note: Says 'I continue today the series that I started', speaks of having lived in Madinah and Makkah, and speaks as the one responsible for the centre and its programmes.
kuGb1M-6KgU.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: The Second Article, Committing Wealth
kuGb1M-6KgU.one_line: Gaza, Myanmar and the cost of silence lead into the second article of the pledge: put your wealth where your mouth is, as the Ansar did.
kuGb1M-6KgU.summary: The third khutbah of his Pledge of Al-Aqabah series was meant to cover the second article, committing wealth, but most of the first khutbah turns to Gaza, Lebanon and a young man from Myanmar who asked him not to forget his people, which left him embarrassed. He counts the days not from last October but from May 15, 1948, and calls the present war one brutal chapter of a long oppression that has woken Muslims to their need for unity, representation and institutional reform. He has no ready solution, but says the Prophet's legacy always offers a way out: the Ansar were a low-status, badly led city whom the Prophet chose because they kept their word. Muslims in the West matter, as Andalus once did, because they can speak for the voiceless; silence and indifference are choices that make you part of the problem, and a comfortable life with occasional fifty-dollar donations cannot be justified. Nothing less than the Ansar's total commitment will work, and there is no luxury for tertiary disputes. In the second khutbah he reaches the article: the Prophet's joy when companions emptied their homes for a destitute delegation, his giving even on credit, and the principle that a community must sustain the centre it uses while the wealthy fund what comes next.

outline.heading: Opening
The pledge: a deal for Jannah
outline.gist: A pledge is a verbal agreement in which each side offers something: the Ansar offered the Prophet five articles and he offered them Jannah, nothing more. The first article was covered last time; today is the second.

outline.heading: A young man from Myanmar
outline.gist: Amid the massacres in Gaza and Lebanon, a young man from Myanmar asked him to remember now and then that his people are still being killed by their government, and he felt embarrassed. Every Muslim soul is equal, and the ummah must feel the suffering of those who get little media attention.

outline.heading: Counting from May 15, 1948
outline.gist: The number that matters is the days since May 15, 1948, about 76 years; everything since is the aftermath of that act of oppression, and the present war is one more chapter of it, more brutal than many before.

outline.heading: A wake-up call for unity and reform
outline.gist: The war has woken Muslims to their dire need for unity, political representation and reform of their institutions and communities. He has no solution, and anyone acting as if they do is posturing.

outline.heading: The legacy always leaves a way out
outline.gist: If we adhere to and live the Prophet's legacy there will always be light at the end of the tunnel, because Allah put enough in His last message for us to find our salvation, and the Prophet performed it himself.

outline.heading: Yathrib: a failing city chosen for its commitment
outline.gist: The ummah has recovered before and is near the bottom of the graph again, which is why he turns to the Ansar. Their city had resources but was being run into the ground by corrupt tribal leaders, had little status and no kinship with the Prophet, yet he chose them because they committed.

outline.heading: Your word was everything
outline.gist: In that society a man who broke his word lost all social, political and ethical standing. The Ansar gave their word and kept it until they died, and that is why Islam reached his own ancestors.

outline.heading: Your presence in the West matters
outline.gist: We cannot escape the images of bombings and killings, but we can adopt a way of life that may prevent this in the future. That is all a Muslim in the West has, and it carries great weight.

outline.heading: Andalus: the ummah's knowledge from outside the heartland
outline.gist: When the heartland was in trouble, Andalus held knowledge of the world and the deen that Muslims later returned to, and many scholars whose books we rely on lived outside the centre of the Muslim world. Never underestimate being where you can be the voice of the voiceless under tyranny.

outline.heading: As long as there is breath in me, the answer is no
outline.gist: Muslims hold beliefs the world wishes they would drop to get in line. As long as he can breathe and speak he refuses to accept the oppression and the corrupt narrative, whatever it costs.

outline.heading: No third option: indifference is a choice
outline.gist: You either follow the corrupt narrative or the one Allah put in His book. Staying silent or uninvolved makes you part of the problem, as the story he has told many times of those who sat back and watched shows.

outline.heading: We inherited this ummah
outline.gist: Everything we do individually and communally is part of the movement of the ummah of Muhammad everywhere; we inherited it and are responsible for its well-being. Having lived in Madinah and Makkah, he knows how divided and indifferent many Muslims are.

outline.heading: The love is still alive
outline.gist: Deep down the seed of love for the Prophet, his legacy and his ummah is still alive in the youth, poorly kindled but not dead; the ummah has not raised the white flag. Keeping it alive depends on Muslims who have the freedom to speak.

outline.heading: No excuse for a comfortable, self-centred life
outline.gist: People elsewhere who can only manage bread, clothing and their children's schooling are excused. Those with freedom cannot justify a life of the car, the house and the trips with fifty dollars here and an hour of volunteering there.

outline.heading: Nothing less than everything
outline.gist: The Ansar offered their lives and their possessions, everything they had, and because of it we are here; nothing less will work for us. Most here did not cause this mess.

outline.heading: Recover the hope that brought you here
outline.gist: Many were driven out of the countries they were born in and landed where they did not know the language, because they believed things could get better. Return to that belief and extend it beyond yourself to the whole ummah you are part of.

outline.heading: No luxury for tertiary disputes
outline.gist: If you are Muslim you chose to belong to this group, and caring for it cannot be a spare-time activity. Until the problem is being fixed he has no luxury to move to other topics, and no one has the luxury scholars had a thousand years ago to argue where to place the hands in prayer while our people are killed daily.

outline.heading: Interlude
The second article: put your money where your mouth is
outline.gist: Having committed to listen and follow him as a leader, not a consultant, they committed their wealth. He knew he could not build a nation or a future if people would show up because it is nice and then walk away.

outline.heading: No one is exempt
outline.gist: Everyone gives, when they have a lot and when they have little, in different amounts; each must look in their pocket and set aside a share for Allah, the community and the ummah. The Quran and sunnah are so full of evidence that it is hard to choose what to recite.

outline.heading: The destitute delegation from Mudar
outline.gist: Muslims from Mudar came to the masjid in clothes stitched together from scraps. The Prophet was upset: they cannot be this poor while we are alive. People brought clothing, money and handfuls of dates until the cloth he laid out was full.

outline.heading: Talk is cheap: his face lit up
outline.gist: His face shone as if painted with gold and silver, because he needed to know his people's commitment was more than talk. That is the pledge: you offer your wealth to the Prophet, not to anyone else, and always spend where the Muslims need it.

outline.heading: Buy on my account: Umar and the Ansari
outline.gist: A man asked a second time when the Prophet had nothing left, so he told him to buy and that he would pay later. Umar objected that Allah had not burdened him beyond his means; an Ansari said give and fear no loss from the Owner of the Throne, and the Prophet smiled: this is what I was commanded.

outline.heading: Something has to give
outline.gist: He died with his war shield pawned, having lent to someone who asked. We cannot hold ourselves to that standard, but something has to give, as it did for the Ansar at their poorest, and our giving must be organized, centralized and accountable.

outline.heading: A community sustains its own centre
outline.gist: Any community that uses a centre or masjid is obliged to support it fully, so that its imam does not have to keep asking the wealthy to cover running costs throughout the year.

outline.heading: Interlude
Support is the measure; the wealthy fund the next step
outline.gist: If people will not support what a centre runs, either they are not being asked properly or it is not useful, and he does not believe in running things people see no value in. The wealthy should be approached for long-term strategy, as the Prophet used them for expansion, advocacy and new institutions, not for closing deficits.

outline.heading: Outro

29:4.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَعۡمَلُونَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ أَن يَسۡبِقُونَاۚ سَآءَ مَا يَحۡكُمُونَ
29:4.en: Or do those who do ill-deeds imagine that they can outstrip Us? Evil (for them) is that which they decide

29:5.ar: مَن كَانَ يَرۡجُواْ لِقَآءَ ٱللَّهِ فَإِنَّ أَجَلَ ٱللَّهِ لَأٓتࣲۚ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
29:5.en: Whoso looketh forward to the meeting with Allah (let him know that) Allah's reckoning is surely nigh, and He is the Hearer, the Knower

29:6.ar: وَمَن جَٰهَدَ فَإِنَّمَا يُجَٰهِدُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَغَنِيٌّ عَنِ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
29:6.en: And whosoever striveth, striveth only for himself, for lo! Allah is altogether Independent of (His) creatures

29:7.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَنُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنۡهُمۡ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ وَلَنَجۡزِيَنَّهُمۡ أَحۡسَنَ ٱلَّذِي كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
29:7.en: And as for those who believe and do good works, We shall remit from them their evil deeds and shall repay them the best that they did

29:8.ar: وَوَصَّيۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ حُسۡنࣰ اۖ وَإِن جَٰهَدَاكَ لِتُشۡرِكَ بِي مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣱ فَلَا تُطِعۡهُمَآۚ إِلَيَّ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ فَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
29:8.en: We have enjoined on man kindness to parents; but if they strive to make thee join with Me that of which thou hast no knowledge, then obey them not. Unto Me is your return and I shall tell you what ye used to do

29:9.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَنُدۡخِلَنَّهُمۡ فِي ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
29:9.en: And as for those who believe and do good works, We verily shall make them enter in among the righteous

29:10.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ فَإِذَآ أُوذِيَ فِي ٱللَّهِ جَعَلَ فِتۡنَةَ ٱلنَّاسِ كَعَذَابِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَلَئِن جَآءَ نَصۡرࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ إِنَّا كُنَّا مَعَكُمۡۚ أَوَلَيۡسَ ٱللَّهُ بِأَعۡلَمَ بِمَا فِي صُدُورِ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
29:10.en: Of mankind is he who saith: We believe in Allah, but, if he be made to suffer for the sake of Allah, he mistaketh the persecution of mankind for Allah's punishment; and then, if victory cometh from thy Lord, will say: Lo! we were with you (all the while). Is not Allah Best Aware of what is in the bosoms of (His) creatures

29:11.ar: وَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَ
29:11.en: Verily Allah knoweth those who believe, and verily He knoweth the hypocrites

46:15.ar: وَوَصَّيۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ إِحۡسَٰنًاۖ حَمَلَتۡهُ أُمُّهُۥ كُرۡهࣰ ا وَوَضَعَتۡهُ كُرۡهࣰ اۖ وَحَمۡلُهُۥ وَفِصَٰلُهُۥ ثَلَٰثُونَ شَهۡرًاۚ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَبَلَغَ أَرۡبَعِينَ سَنَةࣰ قَالَ رَبِّ أَوۡزِعۡنِيٓ أَنۡ أَشۡكُرَ نِعۡمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَيَّ وَأَنۡ أَعۡمَلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا تَرۡضَىٰهُ وَأَصۡلِحۡ لِي فِي ذُرِّيَّتِيٓۖ إِنِّي تُبۡتُ إِلَيۡكَ وَإِنِّي مِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
46:15.en: And We have commended unto man kindness toward parents. His mother beareth him with reluctance, and bringeth him forth with reluctance, and the bearing of him and the weaning of him is thirty months, till, when he attaineth full strength and reacheth forty years, he saith: My Lord! Arouse me that I may give thanks for the favour wherewith Thou hast favoured me and my parents, and that I may do right acceptable unto Thee. And be gracious unto me in the matter of my seed. Lo! I have turned unto Thee repentant, and lo! I am of those who surrender (unto Thee)

31:14.ar: وَوَصَّيۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ حَمَلَتۡهُ أُمُّهُۥ وَهۡنًا عَلَىٰ وَهۡنࣲ وَفِصَٰلُهُۥ فِي عَامَيۡنِ أَنِ ٱشۡكُرۡ لِي وَلِوَٰلِدَيۡكَ إِلَيَّ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
31:14.en: And We have enjoined upon man concerning his partners - His mother beareth him in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years - Give thanks unto Me and unto thy parents. Unto Me is the journeying

31:15.ar: وَإِن جَٰهَدَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُشۡرِكَ بِي مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣱ فَلَا تُطِعۡهُمَاۖ وَصَاحِبۡهُمَا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا مَعۡرُوفࣰ اۖ وَٱتَّبِعۡ سَبِيلَ مَنۡ أَنَابَ إِلَيَّۚ ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ فَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
31:15.en: But if they strive with thee to make thee ascribe unto Me as partner that of which thou hast no knowledge, then obey them not. Consort with them in the world kindly, and follow the path of him who repenteth unto Me. Then unto Me will be your return, and I shall tell you what ye used to do

46:17.ar: وَٱلَّذِي قَالَ لِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ أُفࣲّ لَّكُمَآ أَتَعِدَانِنِيٓ أَنۡ أُخۡرَجَ وَقَدۡ خَلَتِ ٱلۡقُرُونُ مِن قَبۡلِي وَهُمَا يَسۡتَغِيثَانِ ٱللَّهَ وَيۡلَكَ ءَامِنۡ إِنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣱّ فَيَقُولُ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّآ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ
46:17.en: And whoso saith unto his parents: Fie upon you both! Do ye threaten me that I shall be brought forth (again) when generations before me have passed away? And they twain cry unto Allah for help (and say): Woe unto thee! Believe! Lo! the promise of Allah is true. But he saith: This is naught save fables of the men of old

4:11.ar: يُوصِيكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِيٓ أَوۡلَٰدِكُمۡۖ لِلذَّكَرِ مِثۡلُ حَظِّ ٱلۡأُنثَيَيۡنِۚ فَإِن كُنَّ نِسَآءࣰ فَوۡقَ ٱثۡنَتَيۡنِ فَلَهُنَّ ثُلُثَا مَا تَرَكَۖ وَإِن كَانَتۡ وَٰحِدَةࣰ فَلَهَا ٱلنِّصۡفُۚ وَلِأَبَوَيۡهِ لِكُلِّ وَٰحِدࣲ مِّنۡهُمَا ٱلسُّدُسُ مِمَّا تَرَكَ إِن كَانَ لَهُۥ وَلَدࣱۚ فَإِن لَّمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ وَلَدࣱ وَوَرِثَهُۥٓ أَبَوَاهُ فَلِأُمِّهِ ٱلثُّلُثُۚ فَإِن كَانَ لَهُۥٓ إِخۡوَةࣱ فَلِأُمِّهِ ٱلسُّدُسُۚ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ وَصِيَّةࣲ يُوصِي بِهَآ أَوۡ دَيۡنٍۗ ءَابَآؤُكُمۡ وَأَبۡنَآؤُكُمۡ لَا تَدۡرُونَ أَيُّهُمۡ أَقۡرَبُ لَكُمۡ نَفۡعࣰ اۚ فَرِيضَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
4:11.en: Allah chargeth you concerning (the provision for) your children: to the male the equivalent of the portion of two females, and if there be women more than two, then theirs is two-thirds of the inheritance, and if there be one (only) then the half. And to each of his parents a sixth of the inheritance, if he have a son; and if he have no son and his parents are his heirs, then to his mother appertaineth the third; and if he have brethren, then to his mother appertaineth the sixth, after any legacy he may have bequeathed, or debt (hath been paid). Your parents and your children: Ye know not which of them is nearer unto you in usefulness. It is an injunction from Allah. Lo! Allah is Knower, Wise

6:151.ar: ۞قُلۡ تَعَالَوۡاْ أَتۡلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمۡ عَلَيۡكُمۡۖ أَلَّا تُشۡرِكُواْ بِهِۦ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۖ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَٰنࣰ اۖ وَلَا تَقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَوۡلَٰدَكُم مِّنۡ إِمۡلَٰقࣲ نَّحۡنُ نَرۡزُقُكُمۡ وَإِيَّاهُمۡۖ وَلَا تَقۡرَبُواْ ٱلۡفَوَٰحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنۡهَا وَمَا بَطَنَۖ وَلَا تَقۡتُلُواْ ٱلنَّفۡسَ ٱلَّتِي حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ
6:151.en: Say: Come, I will recite unto you that which your Lord hath made a sacred duty for you: That ye ascribe no thing as partner unto Him and that ye do good to parents, and that ye slay not your children because of penury - We provide for you and for them - and that ye draw not nigh to lewd things whether open or concealed. And that ye slay not the life which Allah hath made sacred, save in the course of justice. This He hath command you, in order that ye may discern

6:152.ar: وَلَا تَقۡرَبُواْ مَالَ ٱلۡيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡلُغَ أَشُدَّهُۥۚ وَأَوۡفُواْ ٱلۡكَيۡلَ وَٱلۡمِيزَانَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِۖ لَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَاۖ وَإِذَا قُلۡتُمۡ فَٱعۡدِلُواْ وَلَوۡ كَانَ ذَا قُرۡبَىٰۖ وَبِعَهۡدِ ٱللَّهِ أَوۡفُواْۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَذَكَّرُونَ
6:152.en: And approach not the wealth of the orphan save with that which is better, till he reach maturity. Give full measure and full weight, in justice. We task not any soul beyond its scope. And if ye give your word, do justice thereunto, even though it be (against) a kinsman; and fulfil the covenant of Allah. This He commandeth you that haply ye may remember

6:153.ar: وَأَنَّ هَٰذَا صِرَٰطِي مُسۡتَقِيمࣰ ا فَٱتَّبِعُوهُۖ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ ٱلسُّبُلَ فَتَفَرَّقَ بِكُمۡ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
6:153.en: And (He commandeth you, saying): This is My straight path, so follow it. Follow not other ways, lest ye be parted from His way. This hath He ordained for you, that ye may ward off (evil)

17:31.ar: وَلَا تَقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَوۡلَٰدَكُمۡ خَشۡيَةَ إِمۡلَٰقࣲۖ نَّحۡنُ نَرۡزُقُهُمۡ وَإِيَّاكُمۡۚ إِنَّ قَتۡلَهُمۡ كَانَ خِطۡـࣰٔ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
17:31.en: Slay not your children, fearing a fall to poverty, We shall provide for them and for you. Lo! the slaying of them is great sin

4:36.ar: ۞وَٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُشۡرِكُواْ بِهِۦ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۖ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَٰنࣰ ا وَبِذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينِ وَٱلۡجَارِ ذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡجَارِ ٱلۡجُنُبِ وَٱلصَّاحِبِ بِٱلۡجَنۢبِ وَٱبۡنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَمَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَن كَانَ مُخۡتَالࣰ ا فَخُورًا
4:36.en: And serve Allah. Ascribe no thing as partner unto Him. (Show) kindness unto parents, and unto near kindred, and orphans, and the needy, and unto the neighbour who is of kin (unto you) and the neighbour who is not of kin, and the fellow-traveller and the wayfarer and (the slaves) whom your right hands possess. Lo! Allah loveth not such as are proud and boastful

2:165.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَندَادࣰ ا يُحِبُّونَهُمۡ كَحُبِّ ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَشَدُّ حُبࣰّ ا لِّلَّهِۗ وَلَوۡ يَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ إِذۡ يَرَوۡنَ ٱلۡعَذَابَ أَنَّ ٱلۡقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ
2:165.en: Yet of mankind are some who take unto themselves (objects of worship which they set as) rivals to Allah, loving them with a love like (that which is the due) of Allah (only) - those who believe are stauncher in their love for Allah - Oh, that those who do evil had but known, (on the day) when they behold the doom, that power belongeth wholly to Allah, and that Allah is severe in punishment

67:2.ar: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ وَٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ لِيَبۡلُوَكُمۡ أَيُّكُمۡ أَحۡسَنُ عَمَلࣰ اۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡغَفُورُ
67:2.en: Who hath created life and death that He may try you which of you is best in conduct; and He is the Mighty, the Forgiving

fxvl-V4gYCI.speaker_note: his Friday Arabic tafsir circle continuing Surat Al-Ankabut from the previous week
fxvl-V4gYCI.title: Friday Arabic Tafsir: Surat Al-Ankabut 8-11
fxvl-V4gYCI.one_line: Ankabut 8-11: what saying 'we believe' entails, honouring parents without obeying them in shirk or controlling choices, and those whose faith lasts only in ease.
fxvl-V4gYCI.summary: He continues Surat Al-Ankabut through the idea of the necessary implications of a statement: saying la ilaha illa Allah necessarily brings trials, hope in meeting Allah and lifelong striving, and in return Allah expiates sins and rewards believers by the best of their deeds, then raises them among the righteous. Those who refuse the statement face the same hardships without reward. Verse 8 shows the next trial: parents. He compares the three Quranic wordings of the command to honour parents and explains why each fits its context, and notes that a divine 'counsel' weighs more than a plain command. The Quran commands kindness to parents because people forget them, not care for children which comes naturally. Parents who strive to push a child into shirk must be disobeyed, yet treated well even if they abuse him. He insists obedience covers parents' own needs, not a child's field of study, place of residence or choice of spouse, and warns parents never to use anger or curses against their children. Verses 10-11 describe one who equates people's persecution with Allah's punishment and returns only when success arrives, illustrated by Dhul-Jawshan and Khabbab, and he laments the dead weight in today's ummah.

outline.heading: The necessary implications of saying la ilaha illa Allah
outline.gist: Unlike human positions, the testimony carries implications one cannot drop; the first is that you will be tried so truthfulness becomes evident.

outline.heading: Striving benefits only yourself
outline.gist: Jihad here is general striving against the self and sin, since fighting was not yet permitted; Allah needs nothing from it.

outline.heading: Sins expiated for those who believe and do good
outline.gist: The passage closes with the promise to those who understood what their testimony requires.

outline.heading: Rewarded by the best of what they did
outline.gist: Allah raises all of a believer's deeds to the level of his best and rewards by that, as if only the finest moments were kept.

outline.heading: Those who do evil will not escape
outline.gist: Refusing the testimony to avoid trials brings the same hardships without any reward.

outline.heading: Interlude
Three wordings of the command to honour parents
outline.gist: Ihsanan in Al-Ahqaf, husnan here, and no qualifier in Luqman, matching how many acts of disobedience to parents each verse then permits.

outline.heading: Parents pushing a child to disbelief: among the hardest trials
outline.gist: Here parents push a child from faith, the reverse of Al-Ahqaf where believing parents plead with a rebellious son.

outline.heading: Jahadaka: sustained pressure to commit shirk
outline.gist: Persistent effort by parents to make a child worship other than Allah must not be obeyed.

outline.heading: A divine counsel weighs more than a command
outline.gist: Wasiyya is used for inheritance of daughters and for the ethical commands at the end of Al-An'am, all about treatment of people.

outline.heading: Why the Quran commands care for parents, not children
outline.gist: Kindness to children is natural; children forget what parents did and become busy, so Allah reminds them of what they neglect.

outline.heading: Strive in serving them
outline.gist: The Prophet sent back a man who left weeping elderly parents; Ibn Umar told a man carrying his mother that he had not repaid her.

outline.heading: A line not to cross, and kindness that continues
outline.gist: Obey and honour them in everything except shirk, and stay kind even then.

outline.heading: Accused of dividing fathers and sons
outline.gist: Quraysh accused the Prophet of splitting families, though Islam paired honouring parents with tawhid.

outline.heading: Every command comes with its trial
outline.gist: The surah walks through each command and the hardship attached; no command is entirely easy.

outline.heading: Obedience covers their needs, not your life choices
outline.gist: Parents may advise on a suitable spouse, but may not dictate a child's field of study, residence or marriage for personal motives.

outline.heading: When parents misuse religion against their children
outline.gist: Threatening disownment over personal choices is itself a wrong by parents against children; do not bring religion into such disputes.

outline.heading: Never be angry at or curse your children
outline.gist: A parent who curses his children harms himself, since they are part of him.

outline.heading: Honour them even when they abuse you
outline.gist: Keep your faith and choices but keep honouring parents who insult you; with anyone else you could cut ties, not with them.

outline.heading: Admitted among the righteous
outline.gist: Beyond expiation and best-deed reward, Allah raises the striving believer to the rank of the righteous he had not reached.

outline.heading: Interlude
Some say 'we believe' and are then harmed for Allah
outline.gist: The surah returns to the testimony from a new angle: trial was already established as its consequence.

outline.heading: Equating people's trial with Allah's punishment
outline.gist: Disobeying Allah to escape hardship treats creation like the Creator, like those who love rivals as they love Allah.

outline.heading: Eating haram to escape poverty
outline.gist: Choosing a forbidden way out of a worldly trial equates present hunger with the punishment of the Hereafter.

outline.heading: If victory comes, they say 'we were with you'
outline.gist: In a Makkan surah victory means general success, not military; such people are believers only while things go well.

outline.heading: Dhul-Jawshan, who waited to see who would win
outline.gist: Invited early in Makkah he declined to make enemies; after the conquest he pledged allegiance and bit his hands in regret.

outline.heading: Faith is tiring and demands constant striving
outline.gist: Avoiding haram, generosity, truth before tyrants and justice are its demands; Allah knows what is in every chest.

outline.heading: The sign of hypocrisy: present only in easy times
outline.gist: The first verse spoke of the truthful and liars; this one names the hypocrites who withdraw when sacrifice is hard.

outline.heading: Khabbab: you are a people in a hurry
outline.gist: Tortured on hot coals he asked how long; the Prophet reminded him of believers sawn apart who kept their faith.

outline.heading: The ummah's dead weight
outline.gist: Of two billion, many contribute nothing, cause problems, and appear only when things go well.

outline.heading: Outro

quran.point: Honour parents with ihsan, where no disobedience is mentioned
No qualifier because two acts of non-compliance are commanded
The son who says 'uff' to believing parents pleading with him
Allah counsels you concerning your children, used for the weighty matter of daughters' inheritance
'This He has counselled you with', attached to ethical commands
Do not kill your children for fear of poverty, literally or by depriving them
Worship Allah, associate none with Him, and be good to parents: birr paired with tawhid
Those who take rivals whom they love as they love Allah
Death and life created to test who is best in deed

hadith.gist: A man leaving elderly parents in tears to join an expedition is told to go back and strive in serving them
Ibn Umar tells a man carrying his mother in Hajj that this does not repay her, since she carried him wishing him life
Dhul-Jawshan declines the Prophet's invitation in Makkah, later accepts Islam after the conquest and regrets not being among the first
Khabbab asks 'how long?' and is told earlier believers were sawn apart yet held firm; but you are a people in a hurry

maxims: Every command comes with its trial
Obedience is in their affairs, not your life choices
The ummah is weighed down by dead weight

stories.point: Waiting to see who wins before committing leads to lasting regret.
Persecution is the expected consequence of faith; do not be hasty.

stories.who: Quraysh accusing the Prophet of dividing families
stories.point: Faith can strain family ties, yet Islam commands honouring parents.

contemporary: Parents forcing children into a field of study or blocking suitable marriages for personal motives
takeaways: Accept that faith brings trials and keep striving through them
Honour your parents even if they mistreat you, but never obey them in shirk
As a parent, do not use religion, anger or curses to control your children's personal choices
Never disobey Allah to escape a worldly hardship such as poverty
Stand with the faith in hard times, not only when success comes

29:10.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ فَإِذَآ أُوذِيَ فِي ٱللَّهِ جَعَلَ فِتۡنَةَ ٱلنَّاسِ كَعَذَابِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَلَئِن جَآءَ نَصۡرࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ إِنَّا كُنَّا مَعَكُمۡۚ أَوَلَيۡسَ ٱللَّهُ بِأَعۡلَمَ بِمَا فِي صُدُورِ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
29:10.en: Of mankind is he who saith: We believe in Allah, but, if he be made to suffer for the sake of Allah, he mistaketh the persecution of mankind for Allah's punishment; and then, if victory cometh from thy Lord, will say: Lo! we were with you (all the while). Is not Allah Best Aware of what is in the bosoms of (His) creatures

29:11.ar: وَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَ
29:11.en: Verily Allah knoweth those who believe, and verily He knoweth the hypocrites

29:12.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱتَّبِعُواْ سَبِيلَنَا وَلۡنَحۡمِلۡ خَطَٰيَٰكُمۡ وَمَا هُم بِحَٰمِلِينَ مِنۡ خَطَٰيَٰهُم مِّن شَيۡءٍۖ إِنَّهُمۡ لَكَٰذِبُونَ
29:12.en: Those who disbelieve say unto those who believe: Follow our way (of religion) and we verily will bear your sins (for you). They cannot bear aught of their sins. Lo! they verily are liars

29:13.ar: وَلَيَحۡمِلُنَّ أَثۡقَالَهُمۡ وَأَثۡقَالࣰ ا مَّعَ أَثۡقَالِهِمۡۖ وَلَيُسۡـَٔلُنَّ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ عَمَّا كَانُواْ يَفۡتَرُونَ
29:13.en: But they verily will bear their own loads and other loads beside their own, and they verily will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection concerning that which they invented

29:14.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمۡ أَلۡفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمۡسِينَ عَامࣰ ا فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلطُّوفَانُ وَهُمۡ ظَٰلِمُونَ
29:14.en: And verily we sent Noah (as Our messenger) unto his folk, and he continued with them for a thousand years save fifty years; and the flood engulfed them, for they were wrong-doers

29:15.ar: فَأَنجَيۡنَٰهُ وَأَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلسَّفِينَةِ وَجَعَلۡنَٰهَآ ءَايَةࣰ لِّلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
29:15.en: And We rescued him and those with him in the ship, and made of it a portent for the peoples

49:14.ar: ۞قَالَتِ ٱلۡأَعۡرَابُ ءَامَنَّاۖ قُل لَّمۡ تُؤۡمِنُواْ وَلَٰكِن قُولُوٓاْ أَسۡلَمۡنَا وَلَمَّا يَدۡخُلِ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡۖ وَإِن تُطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ لَا يَلِتۡكُم مِّنۡ أَعۡمَٰلِكُمۡ شَيۡـًٔاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
49:14.en: The wandering Arabs say: We believe. Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Ye believe not, but rather say "We submit," for the faith hath not yet entered into your hearts. Yet, if ye obey Allah and His messenger, He will not withhold from you aught of (the reward of) your deeds. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

4:143.ar: مُّذَبۡذَبِينَ بَيۡنَ ذَٰلِكَ لَآ إِلَىٰ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ وَلَآ إِلَىٰ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِۚ وَمَن يُضۡلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَلَن تَجِدَ لَهُۥ سَبِيلࣰ ا
4:143.en: Swaying between this (and that), (belonging) neither to these nor to those. He whom Allah causeth to go astray, thou (O Muhammad) wilt not find a way for him

4:145.ar: إِنَّ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَ فِي ٱلدَّرۡكِ ٱلۡأَسۡفَلِ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ وَلَن تَجِدَ لَهُمۡ نَصِيرًا
4:145.en: Lo! the hypocrites (will be) in the lowest deep of the Fire, and thou wilt find no helper for them

4:72.ar: وَإِنَّ مِنكُمۡ لَمَن لَّيُبَطِّئَنَّ فَإِنۡ أَصَٰبَتۡكُم مُّصِيبَةࣱ قَالَ قَدۡ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيَّ إِذۡ لَمۡ أَكُن مَّعَهُمۡ شَهِيدࣰ ا
4:72.en: Lo! among you there is he who loitereth; and if disaster overtook you, he would say: Allah hath been gracious unto me since I was not present with them

4:73.ar: وَلَئِنۡ أَصَٰبَكُمۡ فَضۡلࣱ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لَيَقُولَنَّ كَأَن لَّمۡ تَكُنۢ بَيۡنَكُمۡ وَبَيۡنَهُۥ مَوَدَّةࣱ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي كُنتُ مَعَهُمۡ فَأَفُوزَ فَوۡزًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
4:73.en: And if a bounty from Allah befell you, he would surely cry, as if there had been no love between you and him: Oh, would that I had been with them, then should I have achieved a great success

63:4.ar: ۞وَإِذَا رَأَيۡتَهُمۡ تُعۡجِبُكَ أَجۡسَامُهُمۡۖ وَإِن يَقُولُواْ تَسۡمَعۡ لِقَوۡلِهِمۡۖ كَأَنَّهُمۡ خُشُبࣱ مُّسَنَّدَةࣱۖ يَحۡسَبُونَ كُلَّ صَيۡحَةٍ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ هُمُ ٱلۡعَدُوُّ فَٱحۡذَرۡهُمۡۚ قَٰتَلَهُمُ ٱللَّهُۖ أَنَّىٰ يُؤۡفَكُونَ
63:4.en: And when thou seest them their figures please thee; and if they speak thou givest ear unto their speech. (They are) as though they were blocks of wood in striped cloaks. They deem every shout to be against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. Allah confound them! How they are perverted

60:7.ar: ۞عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَجۡعَلَ بَيۡنَكُمۡ وَبَيۡنَ ٱلَّذِينَ عَادَيۡتُم مِّنۡهُم مَّوَدَّةࣰۚ وَٱللَّهُ قَدِيرࣱۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
60:7.en: It may be that Allah will ordain love between you and those of them with whom ye are at enmity. Allah is Mighty, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

60:8.ar: لَّا يَنۡهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يُقَٰتِلُوكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَلَمۡ يُخۡرِجُوكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِكُمۡ أَن تَبَرُّوهُمۡ وَتُقۡسِطُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُقۡسِطِينَ
60:8.en: Allah forbiddeth you not those who warred not against you on account of religion and drove you not out from your homes, that ye should show them kindness and deal justly with them. Lo! Allah loveth the just dealers

9:53.ar: قُلۡ أَنفِقُواْ طَوۡعًا أَوۡ كَرۡهࣰ ا لَّن يُتَقَبَّلَ مِنكُمۡ إِنَّكُمۡ كُنتُمۡ قَوۡمࣰ ا فَٰسِقِينَ
9:53.en: Say: Pay (your contribution), willingly or unwillingly, it will not be accepted from you. Lo! ye were ever froward folk

9:54.ar: وَمَا مَنَعَهُمۡ أَن تُقۡبَلَ مِنۡهُمۡ نَفَقَٰتُهُمۡ إِلَّآ أَنَّهُمۡ كَفَرُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَبِرَسُولِهِۦ وَلَا يَأۡتُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ إِلَّا وَهُمۡ كُسَالَىٰ وَلَا يُنفِقُونَ إِلَّا وَهُمۡ كَٰرِهُونَ
9:54.en: And naught preventeth that their contributions should be accepted from them save that they have disbelieved in Allah and in His messenger, and they come not to worship save as idlers, and pay not (their contribution) save reluctantly

85:17.en: Hath there come unto thee the story of the hosts

85:18.en: Of Pharaoh and (the tribe of) Thamud

31:15.ar: وَإِن جَٰهَدَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُشۡرِكَ بِي مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣱ فَلَا تُطِعۡهُمَاۖ وَصَاحِبۡهُمَا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا مَعۡرُوفࣰ اۖ وَٱتَّبِعۡ سَبِيلَ مَنۡ أَنَابَ إِلَيَّۚ ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ فَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
31:15.en: But if they strive with thee to make thee ascribe unto Me as partner that of which thou hast no knowledge, then obey them not. Consort with them in the world kindly, and follow the path of him who repenteth unto Me. Then unto Me will be your return, and I shall tell you what ye used to do

2:166.ar: إِذۡ تَبَرَّأَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتُّبِعُواْ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُواْ وَرَأَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَ وَتَقَطَّعَتۡ بِهِمُ ٱلۡأَسۡبَابُ
2:166.en: (On the day) when those who were followed disown those who followed (them), and they behold the doom, and all their aims collapse with them

2:167.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُواْ لَوۡ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةࣰ فَنَتَبَرَّأَ مِنۡهُمۡ كَمَا تَبَرَّءُواْ مِنَّاۗ كَذَٰلِكَ يُرِيهِمُ ٱللَّهُ أَعۡمَٰلَهُمۡ حَسَرَٰتٍ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ وَمَا هُم بِخَٰرِجِينَ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ
2:167.en: And those who were but followers will say: If a return were possible for us, we would disown them even as they have disowned us. Thus will Allah show them their own deeds as anguish for them, and they will not emerge from the Fire

35:18.ar: وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةࣱ وِزۡرَ أُخۡرَىٰۚ وَإِن تَدۡعُ مُثۡقَلَةٌ إِلَىٰ حِمۡلِهَا لَا يُحۡمَلۡ مِنۡهُ شَيۡءࣱ وَلَوۡ كَانَ ذَا قُرۡبَىٰٓۗ إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخۡشَوۡنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَأَقَامُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَۚ وَمَن تَزَكَّىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَتَزَكَّىٰ لِنَفۡسِهِۦۚ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
35:18.en: And no burdened soul can bear another's burden, and if one heavy laden crieth for (help with) his load, naught of it will be lifted even though he (unto whom he crieth) be of kin. Thou warnest only those who fear their Lord in secret, and have established worship. He who groweth (in goodness), groweth only for himself, (he cannot by his merit redeem others). Unto Allah is the journeying

12:49.ar: ثُمَّ يَأۡتِي مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَ عَامࣱ فِيهِ يُغَاثُ ٱلنَّاسُ وَفِيهِ يَعۡصِرُونَ
12:49.en: Then, after that, will come a year when the people will have plenteous crops and when they will press (wine and oil)

11:36.ar: وَأُوحِيَ إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ أَنَّهُۥ لَن يُؤۡمِنَ مِن قَوۡمِكَ إِلَّا مَن قَدۡ ءَامَنَ فَلَا تَبۡتَئِسۡ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفۡعَلُونَ
11:36.en: And it was inspired in Noah, (saying): No-one of thy folk will believe save him who hath believed already. Be not distressed because of what they do

11:37.ar: وَٱصۡنَعِ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ بِأَعۡيُنِنَا وَوَحۡيِنَا وَلَا تُخَٰطِبۡنِي فِي ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ إِنَّهُم مُّغۡرَقُونَ
11:37.en: Build the ship under Our eyes and by Our inspiration, and speak not unto Me on behalf of those who do wrong. Lo! they will be drowned

71:5.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي دَعَوۡتُ قَوۡمِي لَيۡلࣰ ا وَنَهَارࣰ ا
71:5.en: He said: My Lord! Lo! I have called unto my people night and day

71:6.ar: فَلَمۡ يَزِدۡهُمۡ دُعَآءِيٓ إِلَّا فِرَارࣰ ا
71:6.en: But all my calling doth but add to their repugnance

71:7.ar: وَإِنِّي كُلَّمَا دَعَوۡتُهُمۡ لِتَغۡفِرَ لَهُمۡ جَعَلُوٓاْ أَصَٰبِعَهُمۡ فِيٓ ءَاذَانِهِمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡشَوۡاْ ثِيَابَهُمۡ وَأَصَرُّواْ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ ٱسۡتِكۡبَارࣰ ا
71:7.en: And lo! whenever I call unto them that Thou mayst pardon them they thrust their fingers in their ears and cover themselves with their garments and persist (in their refusal) and magnify themselves in pride

71:8.en: And lo! I have called unto them aloud

71:9.ar: ثُمَّ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَنتُ لَهُمۡ وَأَسۡرَرۡتُ لَهُمۡ إِسۡرَارࣰ ا
71:9.en: And lo! I have made public proclamation unto them, and I have appealed to them in private

71:10.ar: فَقُلۡتُ ٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ غَفَّارࣰ ا
71:10.en: And I have said: Seek pardon of your Lord. Lo! He was ever Forgiving

71:11.en: He will let loose the sky for you in plenteous rain

71:12.ar: وَيُمۡدِدۡكُم بِأَمۡوَٰلࣲ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ أَنۡهَٰرࣰ ا
71:12.en: And will help you with wealth and sons, and will assign unto you Gardens and will assign unto you rivers

71:13.ar: مَّا لَكُمۡ لَا تَرۡجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقَارࣰ ا
71:13.en: What aileth you that ye hope not toward Allah for dignity

71:14.en: When He created you by (divers) stages

vb7T-HEBHb0.title: Surah Al-Ankabut: The Fair-Weather Believer, Carrying Others' Sins, and Nuh's Long Trial (29:10-15)
vb7T-HEBHb0.one_line: Hypocrites who flee hardship and return for the spoils, why no one carries another's sins, and Nuh as the model of a long trial.
vb7T-HEBHb0.summary: He opens on the theme of striving that frames the whole surah. Accepting death early makes life better: Allah hid our appointed time so we would not procrastinate, and remembering death should improve the heart's devotion without changing sound daily habits, because a person living rightly would change nothing if told he would die soon. Verses ten and eleven describe the person who says 'we believe' but treats people's persecution as if it were Allah's punishment, and reappears when victory brings benefits. This introduces hypocrisy, a mark of Madinan revelation: the two-faced passenger who neither pulls the cart nor gets off it, placed in the lowest depth of the Fire. No one may label a specific person a hypocrite; we should fear it for ourselves as Umar did. When disbelievers offer to carry the believers' sins, the Quran rejects any transfer of responsibility; even soldiers cannot plead orders, and obedience to parents, husbands or commanders is only in what is right. Whoever starts a practice bears its weight along with all who follow it, so start good ones. The prophets section begins with Nuh, whose trial was its sheer length; he understood his test and used every method and the knowledge of his time to call people. Long trials of companions and scholars show how to endure.

outline.heading: A surah framed by striving
outline.gist: The sharp opening exposes those who claim faith; the surah begins and ends with striving because dealing with life's trials is a struggle.

outline.heading: Accepting death improves life
outline.gist: Combat is the hardest form of striving because it risks one's life; the sooner a person accepts his end, the more he values every moment.

outline.heading: Why Allah hid the hour of death
outline.gist: Knowing one's lifespan would feed procrastination; remembering death should deepen sincerity and humility, not change daily routines.

outline.heading: Would you change anything if told you die next week?
outline.gist: If you would change a habit, you are living wrongly now; change it today.

outline.heading: Priorities when death is near
outline.gist: Islamic law limits bequests to a third, so giving away all wealth, quitting work or sitting all day in the masjid shows a misunderstanding of the deen.

outline.heading: Plant the seedling even as the Hour comes
outline.gist: Do the task Allah gave you regardless of outcomes or timing: learn, work, volunteer and serve until you meet Him.

outline.heading: Treating people's persecution like Allah's punishment
outline.gist: The one who says 'we believe' and gives up at the first harm equates worldly trials with the punishment of the Hereafter, which no true believer would do.

outline.heading: "Say rather: we have submitted"
outline.gist: The Bedouins were told they had not yet reached faith; scholars discuss faith without outward Islam and Islam without faith, and only their union is sure of salvation.

outline.heading: "We were with you" when victory comes
outline.gist: He flees trials and returns for the gains, like a poor man who eats haram because poverty frightens him more than the Hereafter.

outline.heading: Hypocrisy: a mark of Madinan revelation
outline.gist: In Makkah people were either open polytheists or committed believers; hypocrites appeared in Madinah once Muslims had power.

outline.heading: The two-faced man wavering between sides
outline.gist: He tells each side what pleases it to benefit from both, belonging to neither.

outline.heading: The lowest depth: the passenger on the cart
outline.gist: He neither pulls with you nor gets off; he is a dead weight and more harmful than an enemy who minds his own affairs.

outline.heading: Truthful versus liar, believer versus hypocrite
outline.gist: The opening contrasted truthful and lying claimants; here it is believers and hypocrites, the type who appears only at mealtimes and trips.

outline.heading: The one who lags behind
outline.gist: When Muslims are hit he thanks Allah he was absent; when they win he wishes he had been there.

outline.heading: Propped-up timber
outline.gist: Hypocrites look impressive like decorative wood but are hollow, and fear every cry.

outline.heading: "They are the enemy", yet never label anyone
outline.gist: The Quran is gentler toward peaceful polytheists than hypocrites, but calling a specific person a hypocrite claims knowledge of his heart; point out the error instead.

outline.heading: Hypocrites unbalance the community
outline.gist: The Prophet counted Madinah's people and wealth, yet half the able men stayed home and the funds did not come.

outline.heading: Umar's fear and Anas's hope
outline.gist: Umar feared being among the hypocrites; Anas hoped to be raised with the Prophet, Abu Bakr and Umar through loving them.

outline.heading: Recitation and tajweed notes
outline.gist: Starting at 'ittabi'u' the connecting hamza takes a kasrah; ma'a is read with a fathah on the 'ayn.

outline.heading: "Follow our way and we will carry your sins"
outline.gist: No accountable person can transfer his responsibility to another; that idea exists in other religions and cultures but not in Islam.

outline.heading: No soldier can plead orders
outline.gist: Modern armies remove the soldier's judgement; in Muslim armies soldiers could refuse unlawful orders, and Pharaoh's soldiers are not excused.

outline.heading: Obedience only in what is right
outline.gist: Obey parents, husbands and leaders in the good only; followers and leaders blame each other in the Fire, and fear of being killed does not justify killing.

outline.heading: Their own burdens plus others'
outline.gist: 'Those who believed' here means those who claimed it; misleaders carry their own sins and a copy of their followers', not a transfer.

outline.heading: Starting a practice: the son of Adam
outline.gist: Whoever starts a good practice gets the reward of all who follow, and the first killer bears a share of every murder.

outline.heading: Start good practices for the community
outline.gist: Filling an unmet need of Muslims with a new service is not innovation in worship, which belongs to scholars to judge.

outline.heading: The first to lead a group astray, and the lie questioned
outline.gist: The first in a circle to smoke or take drugs bears the weight of those who follow; and they will be asked about their false promise.

outline.heading: A new section: prophets and their trials
outline.gist: Nuh, Ibrahim, Lut, Shu'ayb, then 'Ad, Thamud, Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman follow to verse forty.

outline.heading: Nuh's trial was its length
outline.gist: Prophets are chosen here by the type of trial, not by chronology; Nuh's was being unable to finish, staying centuries with a people who would not believe.

outline.heading: Their years may not be ours
outline.gist: The count may follow their calendar; the point is the length, as when Nuh grew trees for decades to build the ark.

outline.heading: A thousand sanah less fifty 'am
outline.gist: Arabs use 'am for a good year and sanah for a hard one; the fifty good years preceded his mission and the rest was hardship.

outline.heading: Nuh understood his test
outline.gist: Even after being told no more would believe, he kept pleading for them; understanding your trial tells you what Allah wants from you.

outline.heading: A sign for the worlds, not a global flood
outline.gist: The Quran says Nuh's people drowned, not all of humanity; the global flood is a claim of the earlier scriptures without proof in Islam.

outline.heading: Calling night and day with the knowledge of his time
outline.gist: Where Nuh lived is unknown, but his story is known worldwide; in Surah Nuh he used every method and drew on the science of his age.

outline.heading: His son and the trials of the prophets
outline.gist: Nuh also suffered his son's disbelief; this section lists prophets with their trials and responses.

outline.heading: Do not complain that your trial is long
outline.gist: No one has waited 950 years; Ayyub is not mentioned here because no trial compares in length, and many scholars endured long hardship.

outline.heading: Imran ibn Husayn, Sa'd and as-Sarakhsi
outline.gist: Imran was bedridden for decades, Sa'd blind for years refused to pray for his sight, and as-Sarakhsi dictated a major work from a well where he was imprisoned.

outline.heading: "If You make my load heavy, strengthen my back"
outline.gist: We are weak, so we ask Allah for gentleness and for the strength to bear what He decrees.

outline.heading: Outro

67:11.ar: فَٱعۡتَرَفُواْ بِذَنۢبِهِمۡ فَسُحۡقࣰ ا لِّأَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
67:11.en: So they acknowledge their sins; but far removed (from mercy) are the dwellers in the flames

67:12.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخۡشَوۡنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ لَهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣱ وَأَجۡرࣱ كَبِيرࣱ‏
67:12.en: Lo! those who fear their Lord in secret, theirs will be forgiveness and a great reward

67:13.ar: وَأَسِرُّواْ قَوۡلَكُمۡ أَوِ ٱجۡهَرُواْ بِهِۦٓۖ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
67:13.en: And keep your opinion secret or proclaim it, lo! He is Knower of all that is in the breasts (of men)

67:14.ar: أَلَا يَعۡلَمُ مَنۡ خَلَقَ وَهُوَ ٱللَّطِيفُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ
67:14.en: Should He not know what He created? And He is the Subtile, the Aware

67:15.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ ذَلُولࣰ ا فَٱمۡشُواْ فِي مَنَاكِبِهَا وَكُلُواْ مِن رِّزۡقِهِۦۖ وَإِلَيۡهِ ٱلنُّشُورُ
67:15.en: He it is Who hath made the earth subservient unto you, so Walk in the paths thereof and eat of His providence. And unto Him will be the resurrection (of the dead)

67:16.ar: ءَأَمِنتُم مَّن فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ أَن يَخۡسِفَ بِكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَمُورُ
67:16.en: Have ye taken security from Him Who is in the heaven that He will not cause the earth to swallow you when lo! it is convulsed

67:17.ar: أَمۡ أَمِنتُم مَّن فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ أَن يُرۡسِلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ حَاصِبࣰ اۖ فَسَتَعۡلَمُونَ كَيۡفَ نَذِيرِ
67:17.en: Or have ye taken security from Him Who is in the heaven that He will not let loose on you a hurricane? But ye shall know the manner of My warning

67:1.ar: تَبَٰرَكَ ٱلَّذِي بِيَدِهِ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
67:1.en: Blessed is He in Whose hand is the Sovereignty, and, He is Able to do all things

67:2.ar: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ وَٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ لِيَبۡلُوَكُمۡ أَيُّكُمۡ أَحۡسَنُ عَمَلࣰ اۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡغَفُورُ
67:2.en: Who hath created life and death that He may try you which of you is best in conduct; and He is the Mighty, the Forgiving

67:3.ar: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتࣲ طِبَاقࣰ اۖ مَّا تَرَىٰ فِي خَلۡقِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ مِن تَفَٰوُتࣲۖ فَٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ هَلۡ تَرَىٰ مِن فُطُورࣲ‏
67:3.en: Who hath created seven heavens in harmony. Thou (Muhammad) canst see no fault in the Beneficent One's creation; then look again: Canst thou see any rifts

67:4.ar: ثُمَّ ٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ كَرَّتَيۡنِ يَنقَلِبۡ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡبَصَرُ خَاسِئࣰ ا وَهُوَ حَسِيرࣱ‏
67:4.en: Then look again and yet again, thy sight will return unto thee weakened and made dim

67:5.ar: وَلَقَدۡ زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا بِمَصَٰبِيحَ وَجَعَلۡنَٰهَا رُجُومࣰ ا لِّلشَّيَٰطِينِۖ وَأَعۡتَدۡنَا لَهُمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
67:5.en: And verily We have beautified the world's heaven with lamps, and We have made them missiles for the devils, and for them We have prepared the doom of flame

67:6.ar: وَلِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِرَبِّهِمۡ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
67:6.en: And for those who disbelieve in their Lord there is the doom of hell, a hapless journey's end

67:7.ar: إِذَآ أُلۡقُواْ فِيهَا سَمِعُواْ لَهَا شَهِيقࣰ ا وَهِيَ تَفُورُ
67:7.en: When they are flung therein they hear its roaring as it boileth up

67:8.ar: تَكَادُ تَمَيَّزُ مِنَ ٱلۡغَيۡظِۖ كُلَّمَآ أُلۡقِيَ فِيهَا فَوۡجࣱ سَأَلَهُمۡ خَزَنَتُهَآ أَلَمۡ يَأۡتِكُمۡ نَذِيرࣱ‏
67:8.en: As it would burst with rage. Whenever a (fresh) host is flung therein the wardens thereof ask them: Came there unto you no warner

67:9.ar: قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ قَدۡ جَآءَنَا نَذِيرࣱ فَكَذَّبۡنَا وَقُلۡنَا مَا نَزَّلَ ٱللَّهُ مِن شَيۡءٍ إِنۡ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ كَبِيرࣲ‏
67:9.en: They say: Yea, verily, a warner came unto us; but we denied and said: Allah hath naught revealed; ye are in naught but a great error

67:10.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَوۡ كُنَّا نَسۡمَعُ أَوۡ نَعۡقِلُ مَا كُنَّا فِيٓ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
67:10.en: And they say: Had we been wont to listen or have sense, we had not been among the dwellers in the flames

10:90.ar: ۞وَجَٰوَزۡنَا بِبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ فَأَتۡبَعَهُمۡ فِرۡعَوۡنُ وَجُنُودُهُۥ بَغۡيࣰ ا وَعَدۡوًاۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَدۡرَكَهُ ٱلۡغَرَقُ قَالَ ءَامَنتُ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِيٓ ءَامَنَتۡ بِهِۦ بَنُوٓاْ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
10:90.en: And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh with his hosts pursued them in rebellion and transgression, till, when the (fate of) drowning overtook him, he exclaimed: I believe that there is no Allah save Him in Whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of those who surrender (unto Him)

10:91.ar: ءَآلۡـَٰٔنَ وَقَدۡ عَصَيۡتَ قَبۡلُ وَكُنتَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ
10:91.en: What! Now! When hitherto thou hast rebelled and been of the wrong-doers

10:92.ar: فَٱلۡيَوۡمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ لِتَكُونَ لِمَنۡ خَلۡفَكَ ءَايَةࣰۚ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ عَنۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا لَغَٰفِلُونَ
10:92.en: But this day We save thee in thy body that thou mayst be a portent for those after thee. Lo! most of mankind are heedless of Our portents

4:18.ar: وَلَيۡسَتِ ٱلتَّوۡبَةُ لِلَّذِينَ يَعۡمَلُونَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَهُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ قَالَ إِنِّي تُبۡتُ ٱلۡـَٰٔنَ وَلَا ٱلَّذِينَ يَمُوتُونَ وَهُمۡ كُفَّارٌۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَعۡتَدۡنَا لَهُمۡ عَذَابًا أَلِيمࣰ ا
4:18.en: The forgiveness is not for those who do ill-deeds until, when death attendeth upon one of them, he saith: Lo! I repent now; nor yet for those who die while they are disbelievers. For such We have prepared a painful doom

6:158.ar: هَلۡ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّآ أَن تَأۡتِيَهُمُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ أَوۡ يَأۡتِيَ رَبُّكَ أَوۡ يَأۡتِيَ بَعۡضُ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّكَۗ يَوۡمَ يَأۡتِي بَعۡضُ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّكَ لَا يَنفَعُ نَفۡسًا إِيمَٰنُهَا لَمۡ تَكُنۡ ءَامَنَتۡ مِن قَبۡلُ أَوۡ كَسَبَتۡ فِيٓ إِيمَٰنِهَا خَيۡرࣰ اۗ قُلِ ٱنتَظِرُوٓاْ إِنَّا مُنتَظِرُونَ
6:158.en: Wait they, indeed, for nothing less than that the angels should come unto them, or thy Lord should come, or there should come one of the portents from thy Lord? In the day when one of the portents from thy Lord cometh, its belief availeth naught a soul which theretofore believed not, nor in its belief earned good (by works). Say: Wait ye! Lo! We (too) are waiting

53:28.ar: وَمَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنۡ عِلۡمٍۖ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّۖ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّنَّ لَا يُغۡنِي مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا
53:28.en: And they have no knowledge thereof. They follow but a guess, and lo! a guess can never take the place of the truth

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

Hr8t5blW5HY.one_line: Repentance that comes too late, reverence as loving fear of justice, Allah's knowledge of the hidden, and an earth made smooth for us to walk and learn.
Hr8t5blW5HY.summary: He finishes the first page of Al-Mulk with the people of Hell admitting their sin, a confession that would have been full repentance in this life, where Allah rejoices at repentance more than a man finding his lost camel in the desert. The door of tawbah stays open until the death rattle or the sun rising from the west, so turn around now. Hell is always paired with Paradise, but mentioned first. Those who revere their Lord unseen combine three things: fear of His justice rather than of injustice, love, and respect, like a loving child who fears disappointing a parent. Verses 13-14 teach that speaking secretly or openly makes no difference, since the Creator knows what He created; al-Latif knows the subtlest details and al-Khabir the unseen thoughts and feelings. After a tajweed note on the hamza, he explains that the earth was made smooth and just right for us, so walk its shoulders and eat its provision. Life on earth is not a punishment: Adam was created for it, and struggle here is how we come to understand Allah's wisdom, compassion and generosity. Those who refuse should not feel secure from the earth shaking beneath them or a storm of stones.

outline.heading: Al-Mulk and the four requirements
outline.gist: The surah protects its reciter and opens a cluster on knowledge, ethics, connection and behaviour; memorize it with understanding.

outline.heading: Recap: the seven pieces of knowledge
outline.gist: Who Allah is, the origin of existence, death and life, reflection, the duality of creation and accountability make up the whole story.

outline.heading: Recap: Hell's rage and the gatekeepers' question
outline.gist: Thrown in, they hear Hell seething and confess that they rejected the warner and would not listen.

outline.heading: They admitted their sin: away with them
outline.gist: Owning a mistake takes courage and would be full repentance in this life, but there Allah no longer listens.

outline.heading: Allah's joy at repentance: the man and his camel
outline.gist: Allah is happier with a servant's repentance than a man who, about to die in the desert, finds his lost camel and misspeaks from joy.

outline.heading: They owned it without blaming anyone
outline.gist: They did not blame the messenger's manner or looks; they said the failure to listen and reason was theirs.

outline.heading: The door of repentance never closes
outline.gist: Provision and other doors open and shut, but tawbah needs no key and is open until the soul reaches the throat.

outline.heading: Too late: Pharaoh's drowning and the sun from the west
outline.gist: Pharaoh believed only when drowning, so only his body was saved as a sign; tawbah closes at death and at the sun rising from the west.

outline.heading: Turn your ship around now
outline.gist: Every moment of this life holds the opportunity to repent and intend better; the Quran repeats this so we do not wait.

outline.heading: A perfect confession no one needed
outline.gist: The gatekeeper only needed to know they had been warned; their honest confession came where it no longer mattered.

outline.heading: Hell and Paradise always paired, Hell first
outline.gist: The Quran never mentions one without the other; you can skip Paradise's details but not what you must avoid.

outline.heading: Khashyah: reverence made of three things
outline.gist: Reverence combines fear of just punishment, love and respect, answering how one can both love and fear Allah.

outline.heading: We fear His justice, not injustice
outline.gist: With people we fear oppression; with Allah we fear being given only what we deserve, and need Him to multiply and forgive.

outline.heading: The loving child who fears disappointing
outline.gist: A child who loves a parent fears letting them down and asks to be let off, unlike a child who fears brutality.

outline.heading: Reverence as the mark of the close
outline.gist: Those near to Allah exalt Him, love Him and fear the consequences of their deeds together.

outline.heading: Revering Him unseen earns forgiveness and great reward
outline.gist: No science will find God; those who built certainty from the signs without seeing Him gain the forgiveness the damned sought too late.

outline.heading: Interlude
Speak secretly or openly: He knows the hearts
outline.gist: Whether hidden or public makes no difference to Allah, who knows what is in the chests.

outline.heading: Assumptions are not knowledge
outline.gist: People can only assume what you hide, and assumption establishes nothing; Allah does not assume.

outline.heading: Does He not know whom He created?
outline.gist: The simplest and strongest argument for His knowledge: who knows you better than your Creator?

outline.heading: Giving birth is not creating: trust your gut
outline.gist: Parents only give birth yet their instincts about their children are usually right, so never ignore them; creation from nothing is far beyond that.

outline.heading: He created existence itself
outline.gist: No one can understand creation better than the One who brought it from nothing.

outline.heading: Al-Latif: knower of the subtlest details
outline.gist: Latif means attention to granular detail, with tenderness as its secondary meaning; He knows what is too small to measure.

outline.heading: Al-Khabir: knower of thoughts and feelings
outline.gist: He knows what leaves no trace, like the small detail in a story that changes its meaning.

outline.heading: Nothing is hidden from Him
outline.gist: All matter and energy belong to Him; to say He does not know is to say He does not know what He made.

outline.heading: An imperative that is not an obligation
outline.gist: 'Speak secretly or openly' does not command either; it means whatever you do, He will know.

outline.heading: The hamza: a heavy, stopping letter
outline.gist: Some letters can be prolonged but the hamza stops dead; much of the difference among the readings concerns how they handle it.

outline.heading: Two hamzas together and stopping on a hamza
outline.gist: Here both hamzas must be pronounced fully, unlike places where the second is eased; stopping on it cuts all sound.

outline.heading: Dhalul: the earth made smooth
outline.gist: The root means low and smooth with no bumps; a servant who humbles himself before Allah has no resistance left.

outline.heading: Just right for you
outline.gist: A globe of water and mountains, yet perfectly suited to us in distance from the sun, size and atmosphere.

outline.heading: You were the goal: walk on its shoulders
outline.gist: Billions of years aimed at humans emerging; we stand on its shoulders and depend on them staying put.

outline.heading: After looking at the sky, walk the earth
outline.gist: The first invitation was to look up; now he invites us to walk mountains, valleys, rivers and forests made for us.

outline.heading: Earth is not a punishment
outline.gist: Unlike narratives of exile, Islam teaches we were created for earth, sent to struggle and learn what compassion and forgiveness mean.

outline.heading: Adam was made a steward on earth from the start
outline.gist: Allah told the angels He would place a steward on earth before Adam's slip; the descent was always the plan.

outline.heading: Eat from His provision; reconnect with the earth
outline.gist: The earth provides everything; modern people are disconnected from it, though we come from its soil and return to it.

outline.heading: A command to walk and eat
outline.gist: Unlike the previous verse, this imperative is obligatory: walk and eat so the friction of life teaches you about yourself and Him.

outline.heading: Struggle teaches the meaning of His names
outline.gist: Making mistakes and guiding others teaches wisdom; being fed by a hungry person teaches compassion and generosity.

outline.heading: To Him is the resurrection
outline.gist: You will return and be asked what lessons you took and whether you emulated His compassion, forgiveness and generosity.

outline.heading: Do you feel safe from the earth swallowing you?
outline.gist: To the one who refuses to walk and learn: what illusion of safety keeps you from fearing the earth heaving beneath you?

outline.heading: When Mother Earth loses her stability
outline.gist: Those who lived through earthquakes know that losing the ground's stability is among the most frightening things.

outline.heading: A storm of stones, then you will know My warning
outline.gist: Or do you feel safe from a storm of stones? Then you would know the reality of His warning.
